body:
FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THIS (server and phone code read 6 Nov 2026, main 068c71a; one claim below was run).

THE SET TO CHANGE TOGETHER. In server/encore_server/encore_server/textnorm.py five functions fold to ASCII and then split on `[a-z0-9]`: `ascii_fold`, `norm_title`, `norm_artist`, `version_signature` (also `[a-z0-9]+`) and `mentions_version`. `norm_key` (refs.py:26) is built from three of them. Their users, which all must keep working on one new normaliser: refs.py (find/resolve, lines 145, 185, 202), navidrome.py:198-210 (`pick_song`), keeper/placement.py:94,105 (`find_existing`, B-13), cover_finder.py:60-73,133, sources/youtube/lean.py:161-173 and scoring.py:96-151.

THERE IS NO TEST FILE FOR textnorm.py. `grep -rl textnorm tests` finds only tests/sources/test_lean.py, and the only non-ASCII literals in tests are in test_lean.py and test_identity.py. That is why nothing noticed (B-37). First deliverable: tests/test_textnorm.py with a native-script table (Arabic with and without harakat, Russian, Greek with tonos, Korean, Japanese, Hindi, Thai) asserting that no key is empty and that two different titles give two keys; and test_refs.py rows for two Arabic songs 1.5 s apart.

THE OBVIOUS FIX BREAKS THREE SCRIPTS (run): replacing `[^a-z0-9]+` by `[^\w]+` splits words at combining marks, which Python does not count as word characters. After NFKC and casefold, Hindi "तुम हो" becomes the tokens त, म, ह; Thai "สวัสดี" becomes สว, สด; Arabic with harakat "كَيْفَك" becomes ك, ي, ف, ك. So marks must be handled on purpose: remove them where they decorate (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic accents; Arabic harakat U+064B-065F and U+0670; tatweel U+0640; fold alef forms and ya, docs/19 section 2) and KEEP them inside words for Indic scripts and Thai (categories Mc and Mn). Separators are then everything that is neither a letter, a digit nor a mark. Put these three words in the test table.

THE PHONE HAS THE SAME FLAW: app/lib/domain/text_match.dart:95 replaces `[^\p{L}\p{N}\s]` by a space, so combining marks become spaces. B-46 ("the phone keeps every script") is true for letters only. Until P2-12 moves matching to the server, fix both the same way or the two disagree again.

DATABASES ALREADY BUILT (decision, with the advisor): `song_ref.norm_key` is stored and indexed (migration 0001, `song_ref_norm`), so every key must be recomputed: a migration that rewrites `norm_key` for all refs. Un-merging is another matter. A merged ref holds the first title only; likes, playlist entries and plays point at the ref, so they cannot be re-assigned by the server. What can be re-derived is the Host's library: each `song_file` has `navidrome_song_id`, so its tags can be read again and the ref split per file. Only test installs exist today (the owner's real server is gate 2, P3-18), so the proportionate repair is: rewrite the keys, split refs by their files, and say plainly in the notes that songs that were only ever streamed are not recoverable. Do not promise more than that.

ACCEPTANCE ADDITIONS: the walk row of P0-13 needs native-script rows, and tools/journeys/ui.py must print Arabic (B-47: `python -X utf8 -I`). Repeat: `python -X utf8 docs/evidence/scripts/audit_probes.py scripts`; real stack: B-37 end-to-end recipe in the register.
